positioning: Adventure always sounds like a good idea.
story: Some dogs ask where you are going. The Siberian Husky has already decided. Eyes blue as glacier ice, tail curled, grin wide, it leans into the cold wind and waits for you to catch up.

The breed comes from northeastern Siberia, where the Chukchi people raised dogs to pull sleds across hundreds of miles of ice. They needed dogs that could run all day on little food. Endurance mattered more than speed, and the Husky has plenty of both.

In 1925 that endurance saved a town. Diphtheria was spreading in Nome, Alaska, and the medicine was 674 miles away. Teams of sled dogs relayed the serum through blizzards in about five and a half days. Togo ran the longest and hardest leg. Balto led the final team into town.
The look is as famous as the history. A thick double coat shrugs off winter. A tail curls like a plume. Those eyes may be blue, brown, or one of each, and every pair seems to be plotting something.
A Husky does not obey so much as negotiate. It sings instead of barking, digs under fences, and treats a closed gate as an opening offer. It needs miles of exercise and plenty of patience from you.
Give a Husky a job, a trail, and a cold morning, and it will give you everything. Joy, mostly. The kind that runs ahead and looks back to make sure you are coming.
rank_cap: The endurance athlete of the north (AKC)
fblocks: Named for Siberia, where the Chukchi people raised the breed. Husky was an old nickname for hardy northern sled dogs.
Togo, who ran the longest leg of the 1925 serum run. Balto, who led the final team into Nome. Both are honored with statues in New York City.
Sheds heavily and needs hours of exercise. Digs, howls, and escapes fences. Not a dog for a quiet life or a short walk.
A dense double coat in every shade from black to pure white. Masks and markings vary. A plume tail curls over the back.
Males weigh up to 60 pounds. The 1925 serum run covered about 674 miles in about five and a half days. Recognized by the AKC in 1930.
days: The Husky curls its tail over its nose. Nature’s built-in scarf.
Huskies were bred to run all day on little fuel.
Huskies howl, yodel, and talk back. Barking is for amateurs.
In 1925, sled dog teams relayed medicine 674 miles to Nome.
Curiosity is a kind of courage. A Husky tests the snowman.
Husky eyes can be blue, brown, or one of each. Ask around.
A pile of Husky puppies is a warm engine of joy.
last_walk:
Breath hangs in the air, and the leash hangs by the door.
A Husky will not wait politely, but it will wait. It stands on the step, bright-eyed, sure that the best trail is the one just ahead. It asks only that you come along. The door opens, the snow glitters, and the whole white world is ready to roam.
